To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Black Spot sediments in sandy intertidals of the German Waden Sea are characterised by increased numbers of aerobic heterotrophic bacteria, which are adapted to the anoxic conditions and high sulphide concentration in the sediment pore water.

the appearance of black spots in the Wadden Sea is linked to elevated organic matter content within sediment, that black spots are characterized by elevated sulphide and anoxia, that black spots contain higher bacterial numbers but lower microbial diversity than control sites and that the microbial communities in black spots are functionally diverse.
Black Spots are characterised by an increase in bacterial numbers and an increase in the number of C-sources utilised.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of anoxia, sulphide and organic matter availability on the structure and functioning of microbial communities in sandy sediments of the German Waddensea.
the effect of anoxia on microbial communities, and the potential for anoxia and sulphide to act as a stressor on aerobic microbial communities in sandy intertidals.
the effects of anoxia, high sulphide concentrations and elevated organic matter content on the heterotrophs in sandy intertidals flats of the German North Sea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Black Spots are characterised by increased bacterial abundances and altered functional diversity of aerobic microbial assemblages.
Black Spots in sandy intertidals flats of the Wadden Sea are characterised by a higher microbial activity and biomass, but lower functional diversity of aerobic heterotrophic microbial populations.
the microbial communities in the Black Spots are adapted to the high sulphide concentrations and anoxic conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the appearance of black spots in the intertidal flats is a natural phenomenon, but it is not a sign of a disturbed ecosystem.
microbial communities at Black Spots are not only adapted to the prevailing conditions, but also benefit from them.
the Black Spot microbial communities are more adapted to the anoxic and sulfidic conditions and are more efficient in substrate utilisation than those of the oxidised control sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Black Spots in the German Wadden sea are not necessarily a negative phenomenon.

microbial community structure in sandy intertidals can be affected by anoxic conditions, but that the effect of high sulphide concentrations is more likely to be masked by the stimulating effect of elevated levels of organic carbon availability.
microbial communities in Black Spots are functionally diverse, with a high capacity for substrate utilisation.
